title: Introduce RAG micro-orchestrator 'Step Inspector' playground and authoring kit
author: Laura Chen
description: This PR introduces a compact RAG micro-orchestrator called 'Step Inspector' — a local-first playground and authoring kit aimed at making multi-tool RAG workflows easier to debug and iterate. Motivation: teams repeatedly tell us that diagnosing where a multi-step agent goes off-track (tool contract mismatch, embedding drift, prompt variant regressions) is time-consuming. The Step Inspector bundles: a) a minimal browser dev UI that renders the step graph, per-step prompt/response, and KV cache snapshots; b) a headless playback runner for deterministic CI smoke tests; c) a lightweight local proxy that can stub tool backends and record wire traces; d) TypeScript and Python adapter examples that show typed tool contracts and structured output checks; e) docs site walkthroughs and a short tutorial notebook. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-2145) - [x] playground UI implemented with minimal dependency set - [x] headless playback runner with deterministic seed mode - [x] local proxy that supports recorded replay and fault injection - [x] sample adapters (ts/python) and one example multi-tool scenario - [x] docs site guide and quickstart - [x] unit tests for core orchestrator logic - [x] lightweight e2e smoke CI job (playwright) - [x] basic telemetry hooks and telemetry-presets presets Notes on scope: this is intentionally lightweight and local-first: it is not a full replacement for the production orchestrator or Dedicated features. The focus is on authoring, deterministic replay, and low-friction debugging for engineers authoring tool-calling RAG flows. The description below summarizes commits, changed areas, review threads, and CI results.
